meta.title: Unipedia — Know what to study now
meta.description: Unipedia knows your semester: it plans your study around your tests, protects your focus, quizzes you on your own notes and shows what actually stuck. For secondary school and university.

hero.kicker: Study companion · Secondary school and university
hero.sub: Unipedia knows your courses, your tests and your notes. Open the app and one thing is waiting: the right block, with the reason why. Finish the block and you know what stuck.

promise.text: and know what to study now.

how.title: One simple loop,
how.sub: Plan, focus, practise, measure. The app handles the boring part so you can handle the studying.

plan.label: Plan
plan.title: A plan that knows your tests
plan.body: Add your exam dates and the time you have. The plan spreads the material across the week, starts the heaviest topics early and tells you when it won't all fit.
plan.detail: It all fits with 2 h a day. I started Calculus a week early.

focus.label: Focus
focus.title: One block at a time, no distractions
focus.body: Tap «Start» and the rest of the world waits. Optional distraction shield, ambient sound and a ring that shows what's left. If you leave, you come back without losing anything.

practice.label: Practise
practice.title: Questions drawn from your own notes
practice.body: At the end of the block, the app quizzes you using your PDFs and slides. You say how it went and it asks again on the right day.
practice.detail: I'll ask you this again on Thursday.

measure.label: Measure
measure.title: See what stuck, not just the time spent
measure.body: Estimated retention per topic and course, reviews due and the weak spots worth your time now. Estimates are shown as estimates.
measure.detail: 3 weak topics before the Physics test

items.title: One decision, not twelve
items.body: At 6 pm, tired, you don't want to choose between twelve cards. You open the app and there's one block, with the reason underneath.

items.title: Three questions, with the right page
items.body: Miss one and the app shows the answer and where it comes from in your materials. Then it asks again.

items.when: On a day that didn't happen
items.title: Nothing bad happens
items.body: A class dinner, the flu, just tired. The next day the plan quietly reshuffles and tells you what changed. You can undo it.

items.title: The time you have, well used
items.body: Not enough for a block, enough for your due reviews. Six cards, including the one you missed yesterday.

mock.name: Sam
mock.why: The test is worth 40% and it's in 6 days.
mock.question: What is the derivative of x² · sin x?
mock.toast: 100 min were left yesterday. I put 50 today and 50 on Saturday; the Calculus test is still covered.

items.title: One decision per screen
items.body: Every screen has one obvious main action. Everything else is a tap away, not in your face.

items.title: No punishment
items.body: Missing a day is normal. No red overdue counters, no streaks lost to the flu.

items.title: Honesty over comfort
items.body: If the material won't fit before the test, the app says so and suggests what to cut. Uni tells you when something isn't in your materials.

items.title: Your data is yours
items.body: Works without an account and offline. The minimum leaves your phone, and you know what and where.

uni.title: A tutor that knows
uni.body: Uni is Unipedia's tutor. Unlike any old chatbot, it knows your semester: your courses, your exam dates and the materials you've added.
bullets: Explains topics from your PDFs, slides and photos.
Builds a plan up to your next test in one conversation.
Says «this isn't in your materials» when that's the case.
uni.chatA: I'd start with Derivatives (25 min): the Calculus I test is worth 40% and it's next week. Then 10 min on the Limits cards you missed yesterday.
uni.chatNote: Based on your plan and your materials

privacy.title: Your notebook
privacy.body: You can use Unipedia without an account: everything stays on your device. If you want to sync between phone and computer, you create an account, and you decide.

items.title: No account
items.body: Local mode on your device, from minute one.

items.title: Offline
items.body: Plan, focus and cards work without a connection.

items.title: You know what leaves
items.body: AI is only used when you turn Uni on, and you're told where the data goes.

items.a: For secondary school and university students, studying in English, Portuguese or Spanish.
No. You can use everything on your device. An account lets you back up and sync your notebook across devices.

items.q: Does it work on phone and computer?
items.a: Yes. It opens in the browser on either one and adapts to the screen.

items.q: Where do the practice questions come from?
items.a: From the materials you add (PDFs, slides, past papers) and your notes. You can also write cards by hand.

items.q: What if I miss a day?
items.a: That's fine. The plan redistributes what was left, tells you what changed and you can undo it.
Yes, Uni uses Google AI (Gemini) and only works once you turn it on. The rest of the app doesn't need it.

cta.title: Your next test
cta.body: Open Unipedia, add your courses and let the plan do the work.

footer.made: Made in Portugal, for anyone who studies.

captions.hoje: Open the app and one thing is waiting: the right block, with the reason why.

meta.title: Study plan — Unipedia
meta.description: A weekly plan that knows your tests, fits back in what slipped and adjusts when life happens. Always with «Undo».

plano.title: Your week sorts
plano.sub: Tell it your courses, when your tests are and how much time you have each day. The plan spreads the material, starts the heaviest topics early and rearranges everything when a day doesn't go to plan.

sections.title: Built around your tests
sections.body: Blocks appear in your week based on the dates and weight of each assessment. You pick the days and the daily goal; the app does the maths.
points: A Monday-to-Sunday strip, with day and week views
Your own rhythm, for example Monday to Saturday, 2 h a day
Every block shows the course, topic and minutes

sections.title: What slipped fits back in
sections.body: A block you didn't do doesn't stay red forever. It shows up under «Left behind» and you choose: fit it in another day, move it to today or discard it.
points: No overdue counters, no punishment
The new plan already counts what was left undone
Always with «Undo» when the plan changes

sections.title: Automatic or manual
sections.body: In automatic mode the plan recalculates when something changes. In manual mode your blocks stay as you left them and the app only suggests.
points: Switch modes whenever you like
«I have 10, 25 or 50 min» on the Today screen
Blocks can be edited by hand

sections.title: Short chats that fine-tune the plan
sections.body: After class, at the end of the day, on Sunday or before a test, you tell Uni how it went, in your own words. It lines up the topics and your next blocks.
points: «It covers up to slide 8 and I've reviewed T01–T03»
Say you're tired and tomorrow's blocks get shorter
Drafts saved automatically

items.title: Add your courses
items.body: Pick your degree and courses, or take a photo of your timetable.

items.title: Add your tests
items.body: Dates and topics for each assessment. You can add them later.

items.title: Let the plan work
items.body: Open Today and start with the first block.

faq.q: What if I don't know my test dates yet?
faq.a: The plan starts with balanced study across your courses and reorganises itself once you add the dates.

faq.q: Can I move blocks by hand?
faq.a: Yes. In manual mode your blocks stay as you left them; in automatic mode every change shows «Plan updated · Undo».

faq.q: What happens if I miss a day?
faq.a: That day's blocks appear under «Left behind». You fit them in, move them to today or discard them; nothing counts against you.

meta.title: Focus mode — Unipedia
meta.description: A calm timer for one block at a time, with an optional distraction shield, ambient sound and an honest record of screen exits.

foco.title: One block at a time,
foco.sub: Tap «Start» and everything else waits. The ring shows what's left, the sound helps you settle in and, if you leave the screen, you come back without losing anything.

sections.title: One ring, one block, one decision
sections.body: The focus screen shows only what matters: the course, the topic and the time. Need more? «+ 5 min». Finished? «Done».
points: Blocks from your plan, or quick 10, 25 and 50 min ones
Pause and resume when you need to
If the page reloads, the block picks up where you left off

sections.title: A distraction shield, if you want one
sections.body: The shield is optional. It puts the app in full screen, keeps the screen on and silences the app's reminders during the block.
points: Full screen and keep screen on
On Android: Do Not Disturb and app pinning
Never counts against your progress

sections.title: Ambient sound to settle in
sections.body: Silence, rain or white noise, generated on your device. Turn it on and off without leaving the block.
points: Works offline
Pick it in the shield panel
Turn it off any time

sections.title: Honest, not punishing
sections.body: If you leave the screen, the app logs the exit and says «Welcome back». If you finish early, your real minutes are kept and the rest goes back into the plan.
points: «Clean focus · 0 screen exits» when it went well
Finish early: keep the real minutes or discard
At the end, go straight to practice

items.title: Pick a block
items.body: The next one in your plan, or «I have 25 min» on Today.

items.title: Tap «Start»
items.body: Turn on the shield and sound if you like.

items.title: Close with practice
items.body: At the end, three questions on what you just studied.

faq.q: Does the shield block other apps?
faq.a: In the browser it puts Unipedia in full screen and keeps the screen on. In the Android app it can also turn on Do Not Disturb and pin the app, with your permission.

faq.q: Do I lose the block if my phone locks?
faq.a: No. The block picks up where you left off and you can tap «Resume».

faq.q: Does leaving the screen count against me?
faq.a: No. Exits are logged so you know, but your progress stays intact.

meta.title: Practice and review — Unipedia
meta.description: Questions drawn from your notes at the end of every block, cards you write yourself and spaced reviews on the right day.

pratica.title: Remembering is what
pratica.sub: Rereading isn't enough. At the end of each block the app quizzes you using your PDFs, slides and notes. You say how it went and it asks again on the right day.

sections.title: Questions from your material
sections.body: Practice uses the materials you've added and your recent notes to create cards on the topic you just studied.
points: 3 to 5 cards at the end of each block
From PDFs, slides, past papers and notes
Also from the «Practise» button on each topic

sections.title: Explain it in your own words
sections.body: Before you flip the card, try to explain the idea without looking at your notes. Then reveal the answer and compare.
points: Reveal with one tap
Hints before the answer
Works even without AI: you write and grade yourself

sections.title: Three buttons, no drama
sections.body: «Again», «Hard» or «Got it». Your answer decides when the card comes back.
points: Again: back tomorrow
Hard: consolidate soon
Got it: moves up the spaced-review cycle

sections.title: Your own cards, offline
sections.body: Write a card by hand in seconds, even without a connection. Due reviews line up in a short queue that fits a bus ride.
points: «+ New card» on any topic
«Quick review» in the Plan
Due reviews in Progress too

items.title: Add your materials
items.body: PDFs, slides or past papers for each course.

items.title: Study a block
items.body: At the end, practice appears on its own.

items.title: Grade yourself honestly
items.body: The app handles when to ask again.

faq.q: Do I need AI to practise?
faq.a: No. You can write cards by hand and grade yourself. AI only helps generate questions from your materials.

faq.q: Where do the questions come from?
faq.a: From the materials you added to the course and the recent notes in your Uni Journal.

faq.q: When does a card I missed come back?
faq.a: With «Again», it comes back the next day. With «Got it», the interval keeps growing.

meta.title: Progress and retention — Unipedia
meta.description: Estimated retention per topic and course, reviews due, study time and the priorities that make a difference before the test.

progresso.title: See what stuck,
progresso.sub: Study time is only half the story. Progress estimates what stayed in your memory, topic by topic, and points to what's worth reviewing now.

sections.title: Your semester at a glance
sections.body: Overall progress, topics finished or reviewed, average, time studied, streak and reviews due, all on one card.
points: 7-day, 30-day and semester views
Reviews due one tap away
No rankings, no comparing with classmates

sections.title: Estimated retention, labelled as an estimate
sections.body: Retention combines time since your last review, your real accuracy in practice and your recall streak. It's an estimate and the app shows it as one.
points: Per topic and per course
Weak topics highlighted
Updates with every practice

sections.title: How much you studied, without guilt
sections.body: A simple chart of time per day against your goal. It's there to adjust your pace, not to punish you.
points: Real time from focus blocks
A daily goal you set
Focus quality: screen exits

sections.title: Up to 3 priorities, not 30
sections.body: Retention and Focus Quality ends with at most three concrete actions: the topic to review, the course to reinforce, the habit to adjust.
points: Each priority opens the right action
Designed for the week before a test
Your Uni collection on the Shelf

items.title: Study and practise
items.body: Every block and card feeds Progress.

items.title: Open Progress
items.body: From the «More» menu, whenever you want the big picture.

items.title: Follow the priorities
items.body: One tap takes you to the right review or block.

faq.a: No, and the app says so. It's an estimate that improves with real practice, not a grade.

faq.q: Is my data compared with other people's?
faq.a: No. Progress is yours alone and is calculated on your device.
The collection of Unis you unlock as you study. It's a bonus; the priorities are what matter.

meta.title: Meet Uni, Unipedia's tutor
meta.description: Uni knows your semester: it explains topics from your own materials, suggests sessions and cards that you confirm, and turns notes into study guides, quizzes and podcasts.

uni.title: A tutor that knows
uni.sub: Uni knows your courses, your test dates and what you got wrong in practice. So it answers what you need right now, from your own materials, and tells you when something isn't in them.

sections.title: Ask like you'd ask a classmate
sections.body: Type, attach a photo of the whiteboard or a PDF, or start from a suggestion. Uni answers at your pace, in a conversation that's saved.
points: «What should I study today?»
«Where am I weakest?» and «My week in summary»
Quick quizzes and explanations with an example and a common mistake

sections.title: It suggests, you decide
sections.body: When it makes sense, Uni suggests an action: a study session, practice cards or a question to take to class. Nothing is saved until you tap «Confirm & save».
points: Study sessions with a day and minutes
Practice cards linked to the topic
Questions saved for class

sections.title: Uni's Notebook
sections.body: Paste notes, add PDFs, photos or a lecture recording and choose what you want: a study guide, a quiz with citations, a quick summary or a two-voice podcast.
points: Citations with the source of every answer
Export as PDF or Markdown
Voice notes transcribed

sections.title: Uni Journal
sections.body: Short chats after class, at the end of the day, on Sunday or before a test. What you share lines up your topics and your plan.
points: Quick replies for when you can't be bothered to type
«Up to slide 8» becomes the test scope
Everything stays in your Progress history

items.title: Turn Uni on
items.body: One tap, and you're told what data goes to Google (Gemini).

items.title: Choose your sources
items.body: One course, all of them, or only the notes you attach.

items.title: Ask
items.body: Or start from one of the suggestions.

faq.a: Up to 15 messages a day are included. If you want more, you can use a free personal Google key, explained in the app.
Yes. That's why every answer has «This is wrong» to flag it, and Uni tells you when something isn't in your materials.

faq.q: Will Uni do my assignments for me?
faq.a: The goal is for you to understand: it explains, gives hints and shows the method. The whole app works without Uni turned on.
